addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- codex:codex-rescue: Proactively use when Claude Code is stuck, wants a second implementation or diagnosis pass, needs a deeper root-cause investigation, or should hand a substantial coding task to Codex through the shared runtime (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- zeroh-roadmap:arc-eval-judge: Scores a LANDED arc's judge-owned eval dimensions (standards adherence, doc brevity, composability/testability, plan quality) from its recorded trace and diff, returning a typed ArcEvalJudgeVerdict with quoted evidence. Spawned by do-arc's eval step and the eval-arc skill; never recomputes a deterministic signal. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Bash)

- zeroh-roadmap:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, pattern adherence, and business rule correctness using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Edit, Write, Bash, WebFetch, WebSearch, TodoWrite, LSP)

- zeroh-roadmap:intent-validator: Independent intent judge — drives the real shipped flow at one acceptance criterion's tier, captures concrete evidence, scores fulfilled intent against a rubric, and returns a typed IntentVerdict. Spawned by validate-arc, one per criterion; never grades work it built. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Bash, WebFetch, WebSearch, TodoWrite)

- zeroh-roadmap:phase-executor: Runs do-phase for ONE phase end-to-end inside an arc and returns a structured PhaseExecutionResult. Spawned by the do-arc orchestrator; never user-invoked. (Tools: All tools)

- zeroh-roadmap:quality-pass: One-shot end-of-phase quality sweep — the merged architect-critique + simplifier pass. Additive half fixes shortcuts, hardcodes, cross-task patterns, and neighborhood issues in touched files; subtractive half deletes dead scaffolding, speculative abstractions, and noise. Auto-fixes in scope; hard-stops on multi-repo / scoped-out / product / speculative. Runs once per phase (reviewScope full only), before the code-review loop. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Edit, Write, Bash, WebFetch, WebSearch, TodoWrite, LSP)
- zeroh-roadmap:references:executor-reference: Agent from zeroh-roadmap plugin (Tools: All tools)

- zeroh-roadmap:software-architect: Designs system architecture by analyzing existing patterns, making decisive technical choices, and producing implementation blueprints. Also the architecture advisor for plan-arc's design-first gate — searches the consumer's arch docs and recommends reuse-or-design (a search-and-recommend role, distinct from the compromise-breaking Decision Contract). (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Bash, WebFetch, WebSearch, LSP)

- zeroh-roadmap:software-developer: Implements features by understanding existing patterns, writing clean code, and following project conventions with a focus on maintainability (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Edit, Write, Bash, WebFetch, WebSearch, TodoWrite, LSP)

- zeroh-roadmap:test-engineer: Writes behavioral unit tests that catch real regressions, enforces coverage on executable logic, and validates that business rules are tested (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Edit, Write, Bash, WebFetch, TodoWrite, LSP)

- zeroh-roadmap:ux-designer: Senior UX design role — designs a surface's layout within the consumer's own UX standards BEFORE it is built, decides per arc whether prose layout reasoning or a static HTML preview is warranted, and returns a recommended UX designRef for the user to confirm. Spawned by plan-arc's design-first gate's UX sub-gate (Step 1b) when an arc has a surface. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Write, Edit, Bash, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- eli5: Explain any topic, code, concept, or error tailored to a specific audience's level of understanding. Use this skill whenever the user says 'explain like I am', 'ELI5', 'explain this to my', 'break this down for', 'dumb it down', 'simplify this for', or asks you to explain something to a specific person or audience type (e.g., 'explain this to a manager', 'how would I explain this to my mom', 'make this understandable for a 5th grader'). Also trigger when the user mentions wanting to understand something at a particular level, or asks for an explanation targeting a non-technical audience. Even partial matches like 'explain to my wife' or 'tell my boss' should trigger this skill.
- goal: Receive and execute a goal dispatched by the lead sentinel (a message beginning with /goal). Acknowledge, plan and execute via the roadmap system, and report halts and landings to the lead by appending a line to your own inbox — the done-report is what pops the lead's queue.
- lead-sentinel: Operate as the fleet's lead sentinel — the voice-connected manager session that dispatches goals to worker sessions, monitors their state, reviews their work, and reports to the owner. Use when this session is the Viky voice brain or the owner asks for fleet status, dispatch, nudge, review of other sessions' work, or what the fleet should work on next.
- codex:rescue: Delegate investigation, an explicit fix request, or follow-up rescue work to the Codex rescue subagent
- codex:setup: Check whether the local Codex CLI is ready and optionally toggle the stop-time review gate
- zeroh-greenfield:brownfield-audit: Handle requests phrased as audit, fill gaps, or reconcile an established repository by proposing only missing, partial, or stale homes before approval.
- zeroh-greenfield:greenfield-init: Handle requests phrased as initialize, scaffold, or create a new repository through an approval-gated setup with sourced stack, design, standards, and roadmap pointers.
- zeroh-greenfield:stack-decision: Handle requests phrased as choose stack, mobile stack, or compare frameworks by presenting sourced alternatives without defaults and returning an ADR ruling.
- zeroh-greenfield:using-zeroh-greenfield: Route requests phrased as init, scaffold, brownfield audit, fill gaps, or stack choice to the owning zeroh-greenfield skill.
- zeroh-roadmap:arc-sweep: Pre-merge sweep for a built arc: dispose every accumulated compromise (reusing release-sweep's debt vocabulary) and run one whole-arc software-architect review against the arc's singleSeams + designRefs, then report merge-readiness.
- zeroh-roadmap:audit-roadmap: Read-only structural audit across roadmap state and the vendored schema (17 checks). Reports findings only — never fixes.
- zeroh-roadmap:do-arc: Execute a whole arc end to end: launch one per-plane workflow at a time, own the halts it hands back, sweep + validate in-session, and land via the CLI.
- zeroh-roadmap:do-phase: Execute a roadmap phase task-by-task with enforced sequential discipline: one task = one commit + a transparencyReport, then the kind-selected gate.
- zeroh-roadmap:eval-arc: Score a landed arc across the seven ratified dimensions — code confidence, verified-vs-intent, standards adherence, doc brevity, composability/testability, speed, plan quality — into a typed, dated ArcEvalReport ratcheted against a rolling baseline. The standalone door onto do-arc's Step 9, for arcs that landed without it.
- zeroh-roadmap:full-code-review: Whole-codebase pre-release audit. Parallel agents cover security, dead code, duplication, performance, architecture, edge cases, data flow, and domain-critical calculations; findings become a release verdict (any critical blocks), a remediation phase, and a review-record round. Use for "full code review", "pre-release audit", a pre-prod checkup on worry areas, or before merge-to-main/prod deploy. Not this skill: diff/phase review (code-review); a consumer's own release-review supersedes this.
- zeroh-roadmap:handoff: Routes unfinished session context into durable roadmap artifacts, leaving only justified residue for a fresh session. Use for requests to hand off work, hand off to a fresh session, continue in a new session, write a context file, or produce a one-line prompt.
- zeroh-roadmap:plan-arc: Plan a whole arc (a named, contiguous block of phases shipped as one unit): author the Arc entity, resolve the design-first gate WITH the user (reuse / new design / inherited ratified prototype / recorded skip), plan every member phase against that design, review each independently, queue one arc tier. Triggers: 'plan arc', '/plan-arc', 'create arc', 'new arc'. Not this skill: one standalone phase (plan-phase) or executing an existing arc (do-arc).
- zeroh-roadmap:plan-phase: Create a new roadmap phase. Use when user says: create phase, plan phase, add to roadmap, new phase, add feature, create task. Reads the code first, pre-makes every decision, rehearses verifies in both directions, then writes and commits a .phase.ts file. Not this skill: planning a multi-phase arc (plan-arc, which loops plan-phase per member) or queueing/auditing an existing phase (review-phase owns the queue).
- zeroh-roadmap:release-sweep: Review and resolve outstanding debts for a release version, then optionally archive the version's done phases. Run before every minor/major; optional before patches. Patch releases are never blocked on debts; archive is.
- zeroh-roadmap:review-phase: Independently verify a roadmap phase or whole arc against the real code: backlog phases get a plan-quality review that repairs the plan and queues it; done/in-progress phases get a report-only post-execution audit. Trigger: 'review phase N', '/review-phase N', 'verify/audit phase N', 'review arc <ID>'; also the mandatory pre-queue pass after plan-phase and the spawned judge step in plan-arc. Not for general diff/PR review or bug hunting - that is a plain diff review (the code-reviewer agent).
- zeroh-roadmap:test-strategy: Test pyramid, coverage targets, and conventions. Use when writing tests, reviewing test quality, or planning test phases.
- zeroh-roadmap:using-zeroh-roadmap: ALWAYS ACTIVE. Phase-driven development plugin. MUST be used when user says: create phase, plan phase, do phase, roadmap, review phase, code review, what's next, arc, sweep, backlog. Routes ALL development task requests through the phase system.
- zeroh-roadmap:validate-arc: Drive a built arc's real shipped flow and judge it against its acceptance criteria with an independent judge panel, reporting PASS/GAPS. The terminal intent gate do-arc runs after arc-sweep, before merge.
- codex:codex-cli-runtime: Internal helper contract for calling the codex-companion runtime from Claude Code
- codex:codex-result-handling: Internal guidance for presenting Codex helper output back to the user
- codex:gpt-5-4-prompting: Internal guidance for composing Codex and GPT-5.4 prompts for coding, review, diagnosis, and research tasks inside the Codex Claude Code plugin
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

Inspect the repository before choosing exactly one route; return the dispatch contract below and do not execute the routed workflow.
Not this skill: delegate routed work to `greenfield-init`, `brownfield-audit`, or `stack-decision`; keep only initial trigger routing here. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-29.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 delivery evidence.

| Request | Skill |
| --- | --- |
| init / new repo / scaffold | greenfield-init |
| audit / fill gaps / brownfield | brownfield-audit |
| stack choice / mobile stack | stack-decision |

```json
{"route":"greenfield-init|brownfield-audit|stack-decision","evidence":["<repository-relative-path>"]}
```

`brownfield-audit`; it preserves existing homes and proposes only gaps.

| --- | --- | --- |

| framework files | absent | framework config or source present |
| existing docs | absent | product, architecture, UX, or standards docs present |

compatibility command. Do not invoke `roadmap init` in any form, including

syntax. Do not write or run a generator. Produce a complete Artifact / Target / Reason proposal, including every
command, dependency/network action, home, gate, and catalog repair. Also emit one

build, e2e, emit. Each non-none gate has an executable command; each absent gate has

event yourself. Stop and await the next invocation.

absolute scratch `cwd`, a complete shell `command`, and an explicit `network`
description. Include full heredoc contents, generator/install/init calls, checks,

seven proposed gate strings must exactly match the config produced after approval.
During execution, run every planned shell command exactly once, in proposal order, and successfully,

shell discovery/checks or combine/split approved commands. Put discovery before
proposal or in the separate read-only audit. Read/Glob/Grep tools may inspect files.

exec_command; Write, Edit, apply_patch, and other implicit file mutation tools are

creation; edits verify approved before-digests and reject unsafe/symlink targets.

form, with strict JSON argument objects: `text(await tools.exec_command({...}));`.

approval response: `APPROVE GREENFIELD PLAN` as a separate input event.

it. Only the outer evidence driver may quarantine the failed scratch tree; an
agent cleanup cannot erase the failure.

success requires raw native tool events and independently observed file snapshots;
model-authored diagnostics alone are insufficient. Run every non-none gate separately with explicit `cd '<scratch>' &&` cwd evidence.

portable configured command and the wrapped native invocation with its real exit. Here `<scratch>` is the absolute observed
consumer directory and `<configured command>` is its exact config binding. Stop on permission denial,
missing sibling, invalid schema, changed existing home, or failing command.

UX canon, harness adapters, README, archetype outputs, catalog checker, and the one
resolved roadmap config. Brownfield receipts separately account for each missing
home, preserve original homes byte-identically, and mechanically constrain the diff

dual-marked roots without creating a second configuration.

second run: audit the completed tree. Require zero proposals, zero writes, and an
identical final tree hash. Emit exactly one native assistant JSON result

finds no remaining gaps; retain actual findings otherwise. Record a separate raw
transcript and tool events. Generate
the human report from validated receipts only. Missing, failed, stale, copied, or
incomplete native evidence remains blocking; never author a replacement receipt.

## Source and evidence driver

Freeze all source inputs before starting the four fresh arms. Obtain the invocation
base and complete dirty/untracked source digest from
`plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-evidence-source.mjs`.

observer request alongside `scratch`, `evidence`, `argv`, `stage`, and `timeout`.

with `host`, `kind`, absolute `scratchRoot`, unique `scratchIdentity`, discovered
`executable`, actual `version`, and brownfield `existingHomePaths`.
After all stages, `greenfield-native-driver.mjs project <empty-claude-arm>
<empty-codex-arm> <brownfield-claude-arm> <brownfield-codex-arm>` validates the
full proof before writing receipts and their Markdown projection. Angle-bracket
arguments denote the four retained arm directories, in the displayed order.
Missing evidence or any failed assertion blocks projection.

## Fixture-selected catalog check

Select the comparator before launching, using `selectCatalogCheck` from the native
evidence module and the reconciliation owner `skills/brownfield-audit/references/readme-reconcile.md`
(relative to the installed greenfield plugin root). For the empty `library-cli`
fixture, bind prospective project-root mode and project name `greenfield-proof`;
verify the generated package identity after execution. For the existing Nx fixture,
bind `node scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs --catalog emitted/repo-catalog.json`
and the existing emitted catalog's byte digest. A workspace wrapper package name
is not the identity of its multiple catalog projects. Refuse missing/malformed
required catalogs; preserve the selected catalog bytes throughout the arm.
Persist `catalogCheck` identically in arm metadata and every observer request.
Include its exact command once in the native proposal and run that comparator once
successfully after approval. Do not run the other mode or report an expected failure
as validation. Retain the selected source file with the other observed artifacts.

## Host build envelope

Resolve `/home/patrik/.local/bin/capbuild` and its canonical path before launch;
bind its SHA-256, default limits, and permitted host effects as `gateWrapper` in
arm metadata and every stage request. Use the same binding for all four arms.
Keep `capbuild` out of consumer `gateCommands`; it is a host execution requirement,
not consumer tooling. For each build, type, unit, integration, and emit command,
propose its actual execution separately using this exact envelope:

```sh
cd '<scratch>' && /home/patrik/.local/bin/capbuild --env npm_config_cache=<scratch>/.npm-cache --env npm_config_logs_dir=<scratch>/.npm-logs <configured-command>
```

Define `<scratch>` as the absolute observed fixture root and `<configured-command>`
as its exact portable gate binding. Use literal absolute cache/log values. Select
portable gate commands without shell operators or assignment prefixes; use
`env TSX_DISABLE_CACHE=1 node --import tsx roadmap/lib/emit.ts` for the fixture emit
gate so transform caching stays disabled across the systemd environment boundary.
Do not change memory/swap/heap/slice defaults, disable locks, add arbitrary environment
options, or run an unwrapped suite inside a compound verification command. Keep
config check and the selected catalog comparator as separate ordinary invocations.

Permit only capbuild's inherited host-control effects outside the consumer tree:
transient user-systemd units and `/run/user/<uid>/capbuild-locks`, where `<uid>` is
the current numeric user id recorded by the driver. These are safety metadata;
they do not authorize any additional consumer path. Record the actual wrapper
command/output/exit and verify the bound executable digest remains unchanged.
The observer clears ambient capbuild, Node, and forwarded test overrides before
launch and records the cleared variable names without exposing their values.

# Brownfield audit

Use this workflow for an established repository. Invoke `zeroh-greenfield:stack-decision` only when stack evidence is unresolved or conflicting, then resolve `skills/greenfield-init/references/standards.md` and `skills/greenfield-init/references/pointers.md` from the installed zeroh-greenfield plugin root as the contract owners. Read `references/marker-table.md`, `references/harness-files.md`, and `references/readme-reconcile.md` when their stages say so.
Not this skill: route initial trigger selection through `using-zeroh-greenfield`, marker-free repositories through `greenfield-init`, and unresolved stack selection through `stack-decision`. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-33.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 fixture and oracle evidence.

## Detect

Confirm the repository root and inspect every evidence glob in `references/marker-table.md`. A marker is evidence, not a stack decision; absence never proves a stack. Inventory existing canonical homes and sibling-plugin availability. Resolve roadmap roots using the marker-table procedure; require the same read-only capability preflight as greenfield-init before proposing config changes. Do not call stack-decision to replace a proven existing choice.

Apply these failure exits:

- zeroh-roadmap absent: STOP and return `/plugin install zeroh-roadmap@zeroh-marketplace`.
- Only when an approved Blade handoff requires it: zeroh-design absent: STOP and return `/plugin install zeroh-design@zeroh-marketplace`. Continue non-Blade documentation and configuration repairs without this sibling.
- greenfield-init absent: STOP and return `/plugin install zeroh-greenfield@zeroh-marketplace`.
- Repository root unresolved: STOP and name the unresolved path.

## Gap table

Expand detection categories into one row per required artifact (PRD, tech-stack ADR, design-system ADR, CODE-STYLE, architecture index, UX canon, README catalog, each harness file, and roadmap config), plus each independently actionable stale/partial asset. Alternative canonical homes count as present; inspect their contents before classifying. Optional framework or Superpowers absence is not a gap unless selected by the approved project requirements. Emit rows with columns `Artefact | State | Evidence path | Proposed action | Existing home to LINK`. Classify each row `present`, `partial`, `missing`, or `stale`; cite concrete evidence. Consult `references/harness-files.md` for harness rows and `references/readme-reconcile.md` for catalog currency.

## Propose

Emit proposals ONLY for gap-table rows in state `missing`, `partial`, or `stale`.
Emit no proposal for a `present` row.
Record approval before any write.

For each eligible row, show the target, source facts, minimal delta, preservation guard, and verification. Do not select a new stack or duplicate an owner contract.

## Approval

Wait for explicit approval of the complete proposal. If approval changes scope, regenerate the gap table and proposal. If approval is absent or ambiguous, STOP with the proposal unchanged.

## Act

Apply only approved gap rows. An existing home is LINKED from the index/canon, never replaced. Follow `skills/greenfield-init/references/standards.md` for conventions and generated blocks, and `skills/greenfield-init/references/pointers.md` for roadmap configuration. Call `zeroh-greenfield:stack-decision` if stack evidence conflicts; never infer a replacement stack.

For harness reconciliation, execute the approved pointer diffs in `references/harness-files.md`. For README reconciliation, use only the checker named in `references/readme-reconcile.md`.

## Verify

Run every approved row's falsifiable check. Re-run the README checker when applicable, byte-compare generated harness marker blocks, and confirm present rows remain unchanged. On any red result, STOP and report the row, command, and evidence without marking it complete.

## Done

Return the final five-column gap table, approval record, changed paths, verification commands and exit codes, linked canonical homes, and any stopped rows. Done exists only when this artifact is complete and every acted row is green.

Emit its parser-bound form with concrete values:

```json
{"type":"audit-result","proposals":[{"path":"<repository-relative-path>","reason":"<reason>"}],"writes":["<repository-relative-path>"],"gaps":["<artifact>: <missing|partial|stale>: <evidence-path>"]}
```

On an idempotent rerun emit empty `proposals`, `writes`, and `gaps`. `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` enforces native event ordering and observed writes; treat gap-only preservation as honor-system. Treat sibling routing, approval interpretation, and every other unbound STOP/ONLY/never rule as honor-system.

# Brownfield marker table

Inspect every row. Evidence supports classification but absence never proves a stack.

| Artefact | Evidence glob | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Package managers | `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `package-lock.json`, `uv.lock`, `pubspec.yaml`, `gradlew` | Present files identify installed package tooling; conflicting locks are partial or stale evidence. |
| Framework files | `next.config.*`, `app.json`, `android/`, `pubspec.yaml`, `vite.config.*` | Framework-owned configuration supports a candidate stack that stack-decision must confirm. |
| Monorepo tools | `nx.json`, `turbo.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `lerna.json` | Existing workspace orchestration is preserved and linked. |
| Docs | `README.md`, `docs/**/*.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` | Existing fact homes are inventoried before proposing a missing index or canon. |
| Harness files | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.cursor/rules/**`, `.codex/**`, `opencode.json` | Apply the harness inventory and generated-block preservation contract. |
| Roadmap config | `roadmap/roadmap.config.json`, `roadmap/phases/`, `docs/roadmap/roadmap.config.json`, `docs/roadmap/phases/`, the explicit `ROADMAP_ROOT` path | Existing roadmap configuration is merged, never reinitialized. |
| Superpowers directory | `.superpowers/`, `docs/superpowers/` | Existing planning artifacts are linked rather than duplicated. |
| Design-system files | `components.json`, `**/components.json`, `tokens/**`, `**/*theme*`, `docs/**/*design*` | Registries and token homes are evidence for design reconciliation, not permission to invent values. |

## Canonical roadmap discovery
Resolve the consumer Git toplevel first. Use `roadmapRoot(consumerRoot)` from the
installed zeroh-roadmap `cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs`; resolve that module from the
installed plugin, never from an assumed consumer-relative plugin directory.
Pass the consumer root explicitly, retain `ROADMAP_ROOT`, and inspect
`<resolved root>/roadmap.config.json`. Do not infer absence from a top-level glob.
A marked root without a config is partial: STOP for an approved recovery proposal,
not fresh initialization. Ambiguous roots STOP with the resolver's remedy; an
explicit override retains the resolver's precedence. If the module cannot be
resolved, STOP the config branch with the sibling installation remedy rather than
implementing another candidate-order algorithm. An unmarked default destination
is not an existing configuration. Record the resolved path as gap-table evidence.

Use this read-only invocation after resolving the two absolute paths from the
installed plugin inventory and consumer Git toplevel:

```sh
node --input-type=module -e 'import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url"; import { join } from "node:path"; const { roadmapRoot } = await import(pathToFileURL(join(process.argv[1], "cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs"))); console.log(roadmapRoot(process.argv[2]));' <roadmap-plugin-root> <consumer-root>
```

`<roadmap-plugin-root>` is the installed zeroh-roadmap plugin directory;
`<consumer-root>` is the consumer Git toplevel. A nonzero exit stops this branch.

# Harness-file reconciliation

Shared invariants belong to `greenfield-init/references/standards.md`; this reference contains only the brownfield delta. The target convention is one canonical `AGENTS.md`, with other harness files reduced to pointers plus genuinely tool-specific material. See `roadmap/arc-prompts/POLYSEAT-execution-prompt.md` for the multi-harness rationale.

For every discovered harness file:

1. inventory its unique material, conventions duplicated from `AGENTS.md`, tool-only instructions, includes, and generated regions;
2. identify the canonical destination for unique material without creating a second fact home;
3. show its exact reduce-to-pointer diff before approval;
4. byte-compare every auto-generated marker block before and after;
5. after approval, retain unique tool instructions and replace only duplicated conventions with a pointer to `AGENTS.md`.

Inventory `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, Cursor rules, Codex instructions, Gemini instructions, and OpenCode instructions when present. Preserve includes and file-local precedence. In particular, preserve the full Nx region from `nx configuration start` through `nx configuration end` byte-for-byte.

If no `AGENTS.md` exists, propose it as a missing gap using the greenfield template. If it exists, link it; never rewrite its unique repository guidance. A pointer-only reconciliation is not complete until the before/after inventory proves every unique instruction survived.

# README catalog reconciliation

`templates/scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs` is the only comparator. Do not implement a second catalog algorithm in brownfield-audit.

1. Copy or resolve `templates/scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs` exactly as greenfield-init specifies.
2. Run `templates/scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs` for the initial red and retain its reported missing and orphan rows as evidence.
3. Propose additions only when the emitted record satisfies `catalog-entry-plus-existing-root`.
4. Treat a README row without a corresponding emitted record and existing root as an orphan. Removal is an `approval-gated orphan removal`; never remove it from detector output alone.
5. After approval, apply only the accepted row additions or removals.
6. Run `templates/scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs` for the final green and attach its exit code to the gap-table artifact.

If the initial run is green, classify README currency `present` and emit no proposal. If the emitted catalog or repository root cannot be resolved, STOP and report the missing source rather than inventing a project.

name: greenfield-init
description: Handle requests phrased as initialize, scaffold, or create a new repository through an approval-gated setup with sourced stack, design, standards, and roadmap pointers.
---

# Greenfield initialization

Use this workflow only after `using-zeroh-greenfield` finds no brownfield
markers. Load each reference only at the step that names it.
Not this skill: route initial trigger selection through `using-zeroh-greenfield`, repositories with existing markers through `brownfield-audit`, and alternative selection through `stack-decision`. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-32.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 initialized-home evidence.

## Read-only compatibility preflight

Before the interview, proposal, approval request, generator, or any consumer write,
require `roadmap` and run `roadmap config capabilities --json`. The response must be
valid JSON with `configVersion: 1`, `scopeManifestProtocol:
"scope-manifest-json-v1"`, and slots `unit-scoped`, `unit-affected`, and
`unit-impacted`. If the command is absent, exits nonzero, returns malformed or older
capabilities, print `/plugin install zeroh-roadmap@zeroh-marketplace` and STOP with
zero consumer writes.
Before approval, run only that named roadmap command; specifically do not invoke `roadmap init`, including `roadmap init --help`. The CLI command-help dispatch keeps `roadmap init --help` read-only; `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` later rejects any observed preapproval mutation.

## Interview

Load `references/prd-interview.md`. Ask one question at a time and retain
unknowns. Do not write the PRD yet.

Invoke `zeroh-greenfield:stack-decision` after the platforms and constraints
are known. It owns the stack alternatives and decision-record text.

## Draft proposal

Load these references in order and assemble a complete proposal:

1. `references/design-system.md` for the design-system choice or sibling handoff.
2. `references/archetypes/<name>.md` for the chosen generator and file shape, where `<name>` is `web`, `flutter`, `android`, `expo`, `nx-monorepo`, or `library-cli`.
3. `references/standards.md` for repository conventions and documentation.

Present every proposed operation in this exact table:

| Artifact | Target | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <artifact-or-command> | <consumer-path> | <why-it-is-needed> |

Include generator commands as artifacts. Cover the PRD,
decision records, design pointers, archetype, standards, harness files, README,
and roadmap configuration before requesting approval.

Also emit this parser-bound object with concrete values and exactly the seven gate keys:

```json
{"type":"proposal","artifacts":[{"path":"<repository-relative-path>","reason":"<reason>"}],"commands":[{"command":"<command>"}],"gates":{"lint":"<command-or-none>","types":"<command-or-none>","unit":"<command-or-none>","integration":"<command-or-none>","build":"<command-or-none>","e2e":"<command-or-none>","emit":"<command-or-none>"}}
```

Define paths relative to the consumer root, reasons as non-empty approval rationale, and `none` as an approved absence with its reason in the proposal table. `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` rejects unsafe, broad, duplicate, or unproposed artifact paths.

## Approval gate

Ask for the exact response `APPROVE GREENFIELD PLAN`.

STOP before any write or generator run unless that exact response follows the
complete proposal. Do not interpret partial agreement as approval. Record the
approved plan and response in `docs/PRD.md §Decisions` during execution.
Treat this gate as enforced by `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs`; other approval interpretation is honor-system.

If a Blade brand requires the design sibling and it is absent, show
`/plugin install zeroh-design@zeroh-marketplace` and STOP that branch. Do not
substitute either sibling's work.

## Execute approved plan

Execute only approved rows through the following headings in order. Run the selected archetype generator first, then write the PRD, decision records, standards, architecture and UX indexes, and harness adapters.

## Structure

Populate README structure from the selected manifest's `## File tree` and
approved `## Generator` and `## Post-steps` outputs.

## Commands

Populate README commands from the selected manifest’s `## Verify` and test conventions.
Resolve `templates/scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs` from the installed zeroh-greenfield plugin root, copy it to consumer path `scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs`, and run the selected manifest checker.
Record its exit code before Done.


## Roadmap configuration

Run `roadmap init`, then apply only the keys from `references/pointers.md`.

Never replace an existing home discovered after approval. Stop with the changed
evidence and draft a revised proposal instead.

## Verify

Follow `references/pointers.md` to execute every non-`none` gate from the consumer root, recording cwd/exit and approved absence reasons. Run the selected archetype's Verify command, the README catalog check, and
`roadmap config check`. Report each command and exit status. A failing command
keeps the initialization incomplete.

## Done

Return Done only when every approved artifact exists, every unapproved path is unchanged,
the approval ruling is in the PRD, the catalog check passes, and
`roadmap config check` exits `0`. Report the artifact paths and verification
results; do not use a prose-only success claim.

After auditing the completed tree, emit `{"type":"audit-result","proposals":[],"writes":[],"gaps":[]}` only when the skill proposes and writes nothing. `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` later cross-checks the claim against independent observer events and tree snapshots; treat other STOP and preservation instructions as honor-system.

## Proposal and approval
Before writing, present `file | source facts | planned sections` for every target and wait for approval. The approved interview, selected archetype, and `design-gate.md` are the only source facts.

## AGENTS.md
AGENTS.md is the sole conventions home. Fill `## Conventions`, `## Don’t`, and `## Generalize-forward`; require Flag-first delivery and keep release-only work in `hold[]`.

## Harness pointers
CLAUDE.md contains `@AGENTS.md` plus harness-only lines. Other harness files point to AGENTS.md and never copy conventions.

## Generated blocks
Preserve generated blocks byte-for-byte, including everything from `<!-- nx configuration start -->` through `<!-- nx configuration end -->`.

## CODE-STYLE.md
Derive code style from the repository's lint and format configuration; do not invent another standard.

## Architecture index
Index the approved architecture records and link to their canonical homes.

## UX canon
Link the UX canon to its design token home from `references/design-system.md`.

## Config branch

## Bind and prove commands
The tables are proposal inputs, not proof that a generator installed a runner.

make verification green. Replace candidate bindings with the repository's actual
commands where needed and retain their source evidence.

#!/usr/bin/env node
import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { basename, resolve } from 'node:path'

const args = process.argv.slice(2)
if (args.includes('--help')) {
  console.log('Usage: check-readme-catalog.mjs (--catalog <json> | --project-root <dir>) [--readme <file>]')
  process.exit(0)
}
const value = flag => { const i = args.indexOf(flag); return i >= 0 ? args[i + 1] : undefined }
const readmePath = resolve(value('--readme') ?? 'README.md')
const fail = message => { console.error(message); process.exitCode = 1 }
if (!existsSync(readmePath)) fail(`nonexistent README: ${readmePath}`)
else {
  const body = readFileSync(readmePath, 'utf8')
  const block = body.match(/<!-- repo-catalog:start -->([\s\S]*?)<!-- repo-catalog:end -->/)?.[1]
  if (!block) fail('malformed README catalog')
  else {
    const tableLines = block.split(/\r?\n/).filter(line => line.trim().startsWith('|'))
    const parsedRows = [...block.matchAll(/^\|\s*([^|]+?)\s*\|\s*([^|]+?)\s*\|\s*([^|]*?)\s*\|$/gm)]
    if (parsedRows.length !== tableLines.length || parsedRows.length < 2) fail('malformed README catalog row')
    const rows = parsedRows.slice(2).map(([, name, root]) => ({ name: name.trim(), root: root.trim() }))
    const catalogPath = value('--catalog')
    const projectRoot = value('--project-root')
    let projects
    try {
      if (catalogPath) {
        const parsed = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(catalogPath), 'utf8'))
        projects = Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : parsed.projects
        if (!Array.isArray(projects)) throw new Error('shape')
        for (const project of projects) if (!project?.name || !project?.root || !existsSync(resolve(project.root))) throw new Error(`nonexistent catalog root: ${project?.root}`)
      } else if (projectRoot) {
        const root = resolve(projectRoot)
        if (!existsSync(root)) throw new Error('nonexistent project root')
        let name
        if (existsSync(resolve(root, 'package.json'))) name = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8')).name
        else if (existsSync(resolve(root, 'pubspec.yaml'))) name = readFileSync(resolve(root, 'pubspec.yaml'), 'utf8').match(/^name:\s*([^\s#]+)/m)?.[1]
        else for (const file of ['settings.gradle.kts', 'settings.gradle']) if (existsSync(resolve(root, file))) name ??= readFileSync(resolve(root, file), 'utf8').match(/rootProject\.name\s*=\s*['\"]([^'\"]+)/)?.[1]
        name ??= basename(root)
        projects = [{ name, root: projectRoot }]
      } else throw new Error('choose --catalog or --project-root')
    } catch (error) { fail(`invalid catalog shape or input: ${error.message}`); projects = null }
    const duplicate = (items, label) => {
      const seen = new Set(); for (const item of items) { if (seen.has(item.name)) fail(`duplicate ${label} name: ${item.name}`); seen.add(item.name) }
    }
    duplicate(rows, 'README')
    if (projects) {
      duplicate(projects, 'catalog')
      const byName = new Map(rows.map(row => [row.name, row]))
      const catalogNames = new Set(projects.map(project => project.name))
      for (const project of projects) if (!byName.has(project.name)) fail(`missing README project: ${project.name} (${project.root})`)
      else if (byName.get(project.name).root !== project.root) fail(`README project path mismatch: ${project.name} (${byName.get(project.name).root} != ${project.root})`)
      for (const row of rows) if (!catalogNames.has(row.name)) fail(`orphan README project: ${row.name} (${row.root})`)
    }
  }
}

=== nx archetype
## Generator
```sh
npx create-nx-workspace@^23 my-workspace --preset=ts --workspaceType=integrated --packageManager=npm --nxCloud=skip --interactive=false
```

Source: https://nx.dev/getting-started/installation. create-nx-workspace is
MIT, tier `Allowed anywhere` as repository tooling.

## Post-steps
Create `packages/`, then add `generators.json` for first-party generators and
`emitted/repo-catalog.json`; the README consumes emitted/repo-catalog.json.
Adopt five Nx tag axes (`type:`, `scope:`, `domain:`, `kind:`, `stability:`),
encode them in `depConstraints`, keep `compilerOptions.paths absent` (no base paths),
and use an Nx-synced solution tsconfig. Preserve `nx:noop` for
intentionally empty targets.

| language option | workspace contract |
| --- | --- |
| TypeScript only | npm workspace packages |
| TypeScript + Python (uv) | npm packages plus uv-managed Python projects |

Not generalized from zeroh: `CODEOWNERS`, `tsdown`, three test runners,
`radix-nova`, and `.building/` coordination state.

## File tree
```text
my-workspace/
my-workspace/nx.json
my-workspace/package.json
my-workspace/tsconfig.base.json
my-workspace/packages/
```

The generated root keeps `libs/` absent until the consumer selects a project.

## Conventions delta
Projects live in `packages/`; boundary tags and `depConstraints` make permitted
dependencies explicit. Repository metadata is emitted, and the README checks
the catalog rather than duplicating it.

## testConventions
Copy `templates/scripts/run-nx-test-tier.mjs` to `scripts/run-nx-test-tier.mjs`.

- Full: `node scripts/run-nx-test-tier.mjs invalid`
- Scoped manifest: `node scripts/run-nx-test-tier.mjs '{manifest}'`
- Affected manifest: `node scripts/run-nx-test-tier.mjs '{manifest}'`
- Impacted range: `node scripts/run-nx-test-tier.mjs '{range}'`

Local exact tests use scoped manifests, phase source changes use affected manifests,
arc inputs use impacted ranges, and CI runs the full workspace sweep. The selector
invokes `npm exec -- nx` with an argv array and fails toward `run-many -t test`.

## designHomes
Set `designHomes.architecture.home` to `docs/architecture.md` and
`designHomes.ux.canon` to `docs/ux-canon.md`.

## Verify
```sh
test -f my-workspace/nx.json && test -f my-workspace/package.json && test -f my-workspace/tsconfig.base.json && test -d my-workspace/packages/ && (cd my-workspace && test ! -e libs && node scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs --catalog emitted/repo-catalog.json)
```
=== design-system
# Design-system step

Choose after the stack ruling and before generation. Record the choice in the
design ADR, UX canon, and roadmap pointers; never invent brand values.

## Web

Use shadcn/ui with Tailwind v4 and its CSS-first configuration. The proposal
must name the component sources and license tier before installation.

Use this `components.json` shape, replacing registry names only with approved
open registries:

```json
{
  "style": "new-york",
  "baseColor": "neutral",
  "cssVariables": true,
  "iconLibrary": "lucide",
  "registries": {
    "@magicui": "https://magicui.design/r/{name}.json"
  }
}
```

Keep one token source and generate the CSS variable projection from it. The byte-check guard fails when generated CSS bytes differ from the token source projection.

Capture `fonts | palette | spacing | ux-canon` as inputs to the UX home. Use
`external-assets-licensing.md §The tiers` to classify every external source.

## beautifului.dev — MIT — Allowed anywhere

beautifului.dev may supply cited copy-paste AI-interface primitives or an
approved registry item. Record provenance with the component proposal.

## Mobile mappings

| stack | mapping | UX inputs | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| shadcn_flutter | Share semantic token names with web and project them to Dart | ux-canon fonts palette spacing | shadcn_flutter |
| Material 3 | Translate semantic roles to Material theme tokens | ux-canon fonts palette spacing | https://m3.material.io |
| react-native-reusables | Project semantic tokens to React Native primitives | ux-canon fonts palette spacing | @react-native-reusables/cli |

## Blade handoff

Invoke `zeroh-design:blade-design` using Path 2. It owns selection and token
values. Store only these approved outputs:

- `designHomes.ux.bindingDesignSystem` points to the sibling-owned theme.
- The `ux-canon pointer line` names that binding without copying tokens.
- The design-system `ADR line` records the choice and owner.

If zeroh-design is absent, print `/plugin install zeroh-design@zeroh-marketplace` and STOP.

## Generator
```sh
npx create-nx-workspace@^23 my-workspace --preset=ts --workspaceType=integrated --packageManager=npm --nxCloud=skip --interactive=false
```

Source: https://nx.dev/getting-started/installation. create-nx-workspace is
MIT, tier `Allowed anywhere` as repository tooling.

## Post-steps
Create `packages/`, then add `generators.json` for first-party generators and
`emitted/repo-catalog.json`; the README consumes emitted/repo-catalog.json.
Adopt five Nx tag axes (`type:`, `scope:`, `domain:`, `kind:`, `stability:`),
encode them in `depConstraints`, keep `compilerOptions.paths absent` (no base paths),
and use an Nx-synced solution tsconfig. Preserve `nx:noop` for
intentionally empty targets.

| language option | workspace contract |
| --- | --- |
| TypeScript only | npm workspace packages |
| TypeScript + Python (uv) | npm packages plus uv-managed Python projects |

Not generalized from zeroh: `CODEOWNERS`, `tsdown`, three test runners,
`radix-nova`, and `.building/` coordination state.

## File tree
```text
my-workspace/
my-workspace/nx.json
my-workspace/package.json
my-workspace/tsconfig.base.json
my-workspace/packages/
```

The generated root keeps `libs/` absent until the consumer selects a project.

## Conventions delta
Projects live in `packages/`; boundary tags and `depConstraints` make permitted
dependencies explicit. Repository metadata is emitted, and the README checks
the catalog rather than duplicating it.

## testConventions
Copy `templates/scripts/run-nx-test-tier.mjs` to `scripts/run-nx-test-tier.mjs`.

- Full: `node scripts/run-nx-test-tier.mjs invalid`
- Scoped manifest: `node scripts/run-nx-test-tier.mjs '{manifest}'`
- Affected manifest: `node scripts/run-nx-test-tier.mjs '{manifest}'`
- Impacted range: `node scripts/run-nx-test-tier.mjs '{range}'`

Local exact tests use scoped manifests, phase source changes use affected manifests,
arc inputs use impacted ranges, and CI runs the full workspace sweep. The selector
invokes `npm exec -- nx` with an argv array and fails toward `run-many -t test`.

## designHomes
Set `designHomes.architecture.home` to `docs/architecture.md` and
`designHomes.ux.canon` to `docs/ux-canon.md`.

## Verify
```sh
test -f my-workspace/nx.json && test -f my-workspace/package.json && test -f my-workspace/tsconfig.base.json && test -d my-workspace/packages/ && (cd my-workspace && test ! -e libs && node scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs --catalog emitted/repo-catalog.json)
```
=== design-system
# Design-system step

Choose after the stack ruling and before generation. Record the choice in the
design ADR, UX canon, and roadmap pointers; never invent brand values.

## Web

Use shadcn/ui with Tailwind v4 and its CSS-first configuration. The proposal
must name the component sources and license tier before installation.

Use this `components.json` shape, replacing registry names only with approved
open registries:

```json
{
  "style": "new-york",
  "baseColor": "neutral",
  "cssVariables": true,
  "iconLibrary": "lucide",
  "registries": {
    "@magicui": "https://magicui.design/r/{name}.json"
  }
}
```

Keep one token source and generate the CSS variable projection from it. The byte-check guard fails when generated CSS bytes differ from the token source projection.

Capture `fonts | palette | spacing | ux-canon` as inputs to the UX home. Use
`external-assets-licensing.md §The tiers` to classify every external source.

## beautifului.dev — MIT — Allowed anywhere

beautifului.dev may supply cited copy-paste AI-interface primitives or an
approved registry item. Record provenance with the component proposal.

## Mobile mappings

| stack | mapping | UX inputs | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| shadcn_flutter | Share semantic token names with web and project them to Dart | ux-canon fonts palette spacing | shadcn_flutter |

values. Store only these approved outputs:

- `designHomes.ux.bindingDesignSystem` points to the sibling-owned theme.

#!/usr/bin/env node
import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { basename, dirname, isAbsolute, relative, resolve } from 'node:path'
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process'

const PROTOCOL = 'scope-manifest-json-v1'
const input = process.argv[2]
const root = process.cwd()
const unsafe = /(^|\/)(package(?:-lock)?\.json|nx\.json|workspace\.json|project\.json|(?:jest|vitest|playwright)\.config\.[^/]+)$/
const testFile = /(?:^|\/)(?:[^/]+\.)?(?:test|spec)\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$/

function full(reason) {
  return { tier: 'full', reason, argv: ['exec', '--', 'nx', 'run-many', '-t', 'test'] }
}

function pathsFromManifest(token) {
  if (typeof token !== 'string' || !token.startsWith('@')) throw new Error('missing @manifest')
  const file = resolve(token.slice(1))
  const ownedTempManifest = basename(file) === 'scope.json' && basename(dirname(file)).startsWith('roadmap-scope-')
  if (!isAbsolute(token.slice(1)) || (!ownedTempManifest && relative(root, file).startsWith('..'))) throw new Error('manifest outside roadmap ownership')
  const parsed = JSON.parse(readFileSync(file, 'utf8'))
  if (parsed?.protocol !== PROTOCOL || !Array.isArray(parsed.paths)) throw new Error('malformed scope manifest')
  return parsed.paths
}

function pathsFromRange(range) {
  if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+\.\.[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$/.test(range ?? '')) throw new Error('unsafe git range')
  const r = spawnSync('git', ['diff', '--name-only', '-z', range], { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf8' })
  if (r.status !== 0) throw new Error('git diff failed')
  return r.stdout.split('\0').filter(Boolean)
}

let selection
try {
  const paths = input?.startsWith('@') ? pathsFromManifest(input) : pathsFromRange(input)
  if (paths.length === 0) selection = full('empty scope')
  else if (paths.some((p) => typeof p !== 'string' || p.length === 0 || p.includes('\0') || p.includes('\n') || isAbsolute(p) || relative(root, resolve(root, p)).startsWith('..'))) selection = full('unsafe scope path')
  else if (paths.some((p) => unsafe.test(p))) selection = full('workspace or test-runner input')
  else if (paths.some((p) => testFile.test(p) && !existsSync(resolve(root, p)))) selection = full('nonexistent exact-test target')
  else selection = { tier: paths.every((p) => testFile.test(p)) ? 'scoped' : 'affected', reason: 'validated scope manifest', argv: ['exec', '--', 'nx', 'affected', '-t', 'test', `--files=${paths.join(',')}`] }
} catch (error) {
  selection = full(error.message)
}

process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(selection) + '\n')
const child = spawnSync('npm', selection.argv, { cwd: root, stdio: 'inherit' })
process.exit(child.error ? 1 : (child.status ?? 1))

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * roadmap — the CLI that owns every repo-state transition (arc ROADCODE). Decisions
 * and transitions are CODE here; judgment stays MODEL. Plain Node ESM, one dep (zod).
 *
 * Universal exit-code contract (honesty rail — exit codes never lie):
 *   0  success / clean / the requested state holds
 *   1  usage or configuration error (missing config, unknown/args, not-yet-implemented)
 *   2  check failed / refused / red (the caller cannot narrate around it)
 *   3/4 long-poll verdicts (watch — 1657) · 5 watch UNOBSERVED (2384.2) · capacity's gate
 *   verdict is exit 3 (at capacity) · role resolve's UNJUDGED refusal is exit 2
 *
 * Commands are cli/commands/<name>.mjs default-export async run(argv) → exit code.
 * A command whose module is not present yet is listed in the tree with its owning
 * phase and exits 1 with an honest "not yet implemented" line — the skeleton shows
 * the whole tree, honestly.
 */

import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
import { ConfigError } from '../cli/lib/config.mjs'
import { RoadmapRootError } from '../cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs'

function printHelp() {
  const lines = ['roadmap — phase-driven development CLI', '', 'Commands:']
  for (const [name, meta] of Object.entries(TREE)) {
    const subs = meta.sub?.length ? `  ${meta.sub.join(' | ')}` : ''
    lines.push(`  ${name.padEnd(9)}${subs.padEnd(38)} ${meta.desc}  [${meta.arc ?? 'ROADCODE'} ${meta.phase}]`)
  }
  lines.push('', 'Exit codes: 0 clean · 1 usage/config · 2 check failed/refused · 3/4 watch verdicts · 5 watch UNOBSERVED · capacity 3 = at capacity')
  process.stdout.write(lines.join('\n') + '\n')

async function main() {
  const argv = process.argv.slice(2)
  const command = argv[0]
  const rest = argv.slice(1)

  if (!command || command === '--help' || command === '-h' || command === 'help') {
    printHelp()
    return 0
  }

  // Help must never execute a state transition, even outside a consumer repo.
  if (Object.hasOwn(TREE, command) && rest.length === 1 && ['--help', '-h'].includes(rest[0])) {
    const meta = TREE[command]
    process.stdout.write(`Usage: roadmap ${command} ${meta.sub.join(' | ')}\n\n${meta.desc}\n`)
    return 0
  }

  const modUrl = new URL(`../cli/commands/${command}.mjs`, import.meta.url)
  if (existsSync(fileURLToPath(modUrl))) {
    const { default: run } = await import(modUrl)
    return await run(rest)
  }

  if (command in TREE) {
    process.stderr.write(
      `roadmap ${command}: not yet implemented (lands in ${TREE[command].arc ?? 'ROADCODE'} ${TREE[command].phase})\n`,
    )
    return 1
  }

  process.stderr.write(`roadmap: unknown command '${command}'. Run: roadmap --help\n`)
  return 1
}

try {
  process.exit(await main())
} catch (e) {
  // Both carry messageLines and both are REFUSALS the operator can act on — an ambiguous
  // root reached through any door (status, audit, claim, gate…) must read as one named
  // message with its remedy, never as a stack trace the reader has to decode.
  if (e instanceof ConfigError || e instanceof RoadmapRootError) {
    for (const line of e.messageLines) process.stderr.write(line + '\n')
    process.exit(1)
  }
  process.stderr.write(`roadmap: ${e?.stack ?? e}\n`)
  process.exit(1)
}

/**
 * roadmap-root — THE answer to "where is this consumer's roadmap?", and the ONLY module
 * under cli/ or hooks/ allowed to spell the root as a literal (cli/lib/roadmap-root.test.mjs
 * scans for it; every other site joins onto what these functions return).
 *
 * Two homes, discovered rather than configured: the config lives INSIDE the root, so a
 * roadmap.config.json key could never name it. `roadmap/` at the git toplevel is what every
 * consumer has today and stays first; `docs/roadmap/` is the second candidate, for a repo that
 * keeps its workflows as sibling doc folders (docs/roadmap/ beside docs/superpowers/).
 *
 * The rules, in order:
 *  - ROADMAP_ROOT wins, absolute or resolved against `dir`, and is NOT probed — an override
 *    names where the root WILL be, so `roadmap init` can scaffold into it.
 *  - else the first candidate carrying a MARKER (roadmap.config.json or phases/). An existing
 *    but unmarked directory is not a marker: a repo with a prose docs/roadmap/ folder must
 *    keep reading its real roadmap/.
 *  - both marked → RoadmapRootError('ambiguous'), never a silent pick. Two roots means two
 *    backlogs, two claim registries and two gate directories; guessing one is how half a
 *    consumer's records go quietly unread.
 *  - neither marked → the default first candidate, so a fresh or non-consumer tree answers
 *    exactly what it answered before this module existed.
 *
 * SHELL TWIN: hooks/lib/roadmap-root.sh implements the same three rules for the hooks, which
 * cannot afford to spawn node on every tool call. A change here is a change there. It differs in
 * FORM only on ambiguity — it returns non-zero after one stderr line instead of throwing, because
 * a hook must never block a session — and in neither case does either twin GUESS a root.
 */
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join, resolve, relative, isAbsolute, sep } from 'node:path'
import { BridgeError } from './bridge-error.mjs'
import { gitToplevel } from './gitroot.mjs'

/** The root homes, in PRECEDENCE order. Extending this list extends discovery everywhere. */
export const ROOT_CANDIDATES = ['roadmap', 'docs/roadmap']

/** What makes a candidate directory a roadmap root rather than a same-named prose folder. */
const MARKERS = ['roadmap.config.json', 'phases']

/** Typed root-resolution failure. kind ∈ 'ambiguous'. Same shape as ConfigError. */
export class RoadmapRootError extends Error {
  constructor(kind, messageLines) {
    super(messageLines.join('\n'))
    this.name = 'RoadmapRootError'
    this.kind = kind
    this.messageLines = messageLines
  }
}

/** [dir, override] → resolved root. Keyed on both: a memo keyed on dir alone
 *  would hand a later caller an answer the current ROADMAP_ROOT never authorized. */
const memo = new Map()

/**
 * Drop every memoized resolution. For tests and long-lived processes that MUTATE a tree
 * (scaffolding a root, then resolving it) — the probes are fs reads, and a cached miss
 * outlives the directory that caused it.
 */
export function resetRoadmapRootCache() {
  memo.clear()
}

/** The override in force, or null. An empty ROADMAP_ROOT is unset, not "the cwd". */
function override() {
  const raw = process.env.ROADMAP_ROOT
  return raw != null && raw !== '' ? raw : null
}

const isRoot = (candidateDir) => MARKERS.some((m) => existsSync(join(candidateDir, m)))

/**
 * The consumer's roadmap data root for the tree at `dir` (normally a git toplevel).
 * @param {string} dir
 * @returns {string} an ABSOLUTE directory path
 * @throws {RoadmapRootError} kind 'ambiguous' when more than one candidate is marked
 */
export function roadmapRoot(dir) {
  const env = override()
  const key = JSON.stringify([dir, env])
  const hit = memo.get(key)
  if (hit !== undefined) return hit

  // The override is checked BEFORE the ambiguity refusal on purpose: it is the remedy that
  // refusal advertises, and a remedy resolved after the throw could never be taken.
  const resolved = env ? (isAbsolute(env) ? env : resolve(dir, env)) : probe(dir)
  memo.set(key, resolved)
  return resolved
}

function probe(dir) {
  const marked = ROOT_CANDIDATES.map((c) => resolve(dir, c)).filter(isRoot)
  if (marked.length > 1) {
    throw new RoadmapRootError('ambiguous', [
      `roadmap: ${dir} carries more than one roadmap root — ${marked.join(' and ')}`,
      `each holds its own records, so reading either one silently hides the other. Delete or merge the one that is not yours, or name the real root: ROADMAP_ROOT=<dir> roadmap <command>`,
    ])
  }
  return marked[0] ?? resolve(dir, ROOT_CANDIDATES[0])
}

/**
 * The root a FLAGLESS `roadmap status` / `roadmap claim` reads: the consumer's resolved root.
 * Outside a git repo — where both commands still accept a bare roadmap directory — the
 * candidate under `cwd`.
 *
 * ONLY the not-a-repo case falls back. A RoadmapRootError must ESCAPE: falling back on an
 * ambiguous tree would resolve `<cwd>/roadmap` and silently pick one of the two roots the
 * refusal exists to prevent — and from a SUBDIRECTORY it would invent a root that is not
 * there at all.
 * @param {string} cwd
 * @returns {string} an ABSOLUTE directory path
 * @throws {RoadmapRootError} kind 'ambiguous', unchanged, from either branch
 */
export function defaultRoadmapRoot(cwd) {
  let toplevel
  try {
    toplevel = gitToplevel(cwd)
  } catch {
    return roadmapRoot(cwd)
  }
  return roadmapRoot(toplevel)
}

/**
 * The same answer spelled RELATIVE to `dir`, POSIX-separated and with no trailing slash —
 * what git pathspecs (`git log -- <rel>/backlog.ts`), diff-path prefix tests and the
 * repo-relative provenance strings cited in eval reports all need. Throws exactly where
 * roadmapRoot throws: an ambiguous tree must never be handed a guessed pathspec.
 * @param {string} dir
 * @returns {string} e.g. 'roadmap' or 'docs/roadmap'
 */
export function roadmapRootRel(dir) {
  const rel = relative(dir, roadmapRoot(dir))
  return sep === '/' ? rel : rel.split(sep).join('/')
}

/**
 * The consumer's vendored schema seam — what the tsx bridge validates every typed roadmap
 * file through. Root-first (`<root>/lib/schema.ts`, what a consumer scaffolded from now on
 * carries, reachable by a relative import with no tsconfig alias), then the LEGACY
 * `<dir>/lib/roadmap/schema.ts` that every existing consumer still has.
 * @param {string} dir  a consumer root (git toplevel)
 * @returns {string} an absolute path to an existing file
 * @throws {BridgeError} kind 'schema-missing', naming BOTH candidates
 */
export function consumerSchemaPath(dir) {
  const rootSeam = join(roadmapRoot(dir), 'lib', 'schema.ts')
  if (existsSync(rootSeam)) return rootSeam
  const legacySeam = join(dir, 'lib', 'roadmap', 'schema.ts')
  if (existsSync(legacySeam)) return legacySeam
  throw new BridgeError('schema-missing', [
    `roadmap: no consumer schema at ${rootSeam} (nor at the legacy seam ${legacySeam}) — this repo is not a roadmap consumer`,
  ])
}

import { gitToplevel } from './gitroot.mjs'

/** What makes a candidate directory a roadmap root rather than a same-named prose folder. */
const MARKERS = ['roadmap.config.json', 'phases']

/** Typed root-resolution failure. kind ∈ 'ambiguous'. Same shape as ConfigError. */
export class RoadmapRootError extends Error {
  constructor(kind, messageLines) {
    super(messageLines.join('\n'))
    this.name = 'RoadmapRootError'
    this.kind = kind
    this.messageLines = messageLines

 * outlives the directory that caused it.

export function resetRoadmapRootCache() {
  memo.clear()

function override() {
  const raw = process.env.ROADMAP_ROOT

}

 * The consumer's roadmap data root for the tree at `dir` (normally a git toplevel).
 * @param {string} dir

 * @throws {RoadmapRootError} kind 'ambiguous' when more than one candidate is marked

export function roadmapRoot(dir) {

  const hit = memo.get(key)
  if (hit !== undefined) return hit

  // refusal advertises, and a remedy resolved after the throw could never be taken.
  const resolved = env ? (isAbsolute(env) ? env : resolve(dir, env)) : probe(dir)

 * Outside a git repo — where both commands still accept a bare roadmap directory — the

  const legacySeam = join(dir, 'lib', 'roadmap', 'schema.ts')

    `roadmap: no consumer schema at ${rootSeam} (nor at the legacy seam ${legacySeam}) — this repo is not a roadmap consumer`,

# ADR 0001: Technology stack

## Status

Accepted

## Date

2026-09-05

## Context

The repository is an existing npm-managed Nx workspace: `package.json` declares `nx ^23` with no lockfile and no installed `node_modules`; `nx.json` has empty `targetDefaults`; `apps/web`, `apps/api`, `apps/admin`, `packages/shared`, `packages/ui`, and `packages/generators` each carry a `project.json` without targets. The workspace is structural; no runtime, test runner, or build tooling is present. Private, non-Blade, no mobile, no product remote or deployment.

## Options
| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Retain the existing Nx workspace as-is | Preserves evidenced structure and boundaries; no invented tooling | Apps remain non-runnable until a runtime is chosen | The repository is structural and the product runtime is undecided | Shared packages already modelled as Nx libraries | `nx.json`, `package.json` |
| Select a runtime stack now | Enables runnable targets and gates | Requires product facts that are unknown; would replace a proven existing choice | Product runtime requirements are known | Depends on the selected stack | not evidenced |

## Ruling

2026-09-05: Retain the existing Nx workspace — it is the proven evidenced choice; a runtime stack is not selected because the fixture provides no product facts and no runnable targets, and stack-decision is deferred until requirements exist.

## Consequences

- Positive: existing homes and boundaries are preserved; the architecture index links them.
- Negative: every quality gate is declared absent (`none`) in `roadmap/roadmap.config.json` until tooling is actually installed.

## Revisit when

A runtime is selected for any app, a lockfile or `node_modules` appears, or any `project.json` gains an executable target.

Unknown. The repository is a structural Nx workspace; no product statement exists in any inventoried home (`README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture/`). The unknown is preserved, not invented.

=================== docs/adr/0001-tech-stack.md
# ADR 0001: Technology stack

## Status

Accepted

## Date

2026-09-05

## Context

The repository is an existing npm-managed Nx workspace: `package.json` (`zeroh-shaped-fixture`, private) declares only `nx ^23.0.0` as a devDependency, with no lockfile and no installed `node_modules`; `nx.json` has empty `targetDefaults`; `apps/web`, `apps/api`, `apps/admin`, `packages/shared`, `packages/ui` and `packages/generators` each carry a `project.json` naming only `name`, `root` and `projectType`, with no targets. No framework configuration (`next.config.*`, `vite.config.*`, `app.json`, `android/`, `pubspec.yaml`) exists. The workspace is structural; no runtime, test runner or build tooling is present. Private, unlicensed, non-Blade, no mobile, no product remote or deployment.

## Options
| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Retain the existing Nx workspace as-is | Preserves the evidenced structure and boundaries; invents no tooling | Apps stay non-runnable until a runtime is chosen | The repository is structural and the product runtime is undecided | Shared packages are already modelled as Nx libraries | `nx.json`, `package.json`, `apps/*/project.json`, `packages/*/project.json` |
| Select a runtime stack now via stack-decision | Enables runnable targets and real gates | Requires product facts that are unknown and would replace a proven existing choice | Product runtime requirements are known | Depends on the selected stack | not evidenced |

## Ruling

2026-09-05: Retain the existing Nx workspace. It is the proven evidenced choice; no runtime stack is selected because the repository provides no product facts and no runnable targets, and `stack-decision` is deferred until requirements exist.

## Consequences

- Positive: existing homes and boundaries are preserved; `docs/architecture.md` links them.
- Negative: every quality gate is declared absent (`none`) in `roadmap/roadmap.config.json` until tooling is actually installed and bound.

## Revisit when

A runtime is selected for any app, a lockfile or `node_modules` appears, or any `project.json` gains an executable target.

# ADR 0002: Design system

## Status

Accepted

## Date

2026-09-05

## Context

`apps/web/components.json` and `packages/ui/components.json` both declare `{"style":"new-york","tsx":true}` with no registries, base color, CSS variables or icon library. No token home, theme or design documentation exists (`tokens/`, `*theme*`, `docs/**/*design*` are all absent). The repository is non-Blade, so no zeroh-design sibling handoff applies. No brand values are known.

## Options
| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Record the existing shadcn-style `components.json` evidence with registry none | Matches evidenced files; invents nothing | Leaves palette, fonts and registries undecided | Brand and product facts are unknown | Components remain source-owned in `packages/ui` | `apps/web/components.json`, `packages/ui/components.json` |
| Select a registry and token source now | Completes the design system | Requires brand inputs that do not exist | Brand values are supplied | Registry items compose locally | not evidenced |

## Ruling

2026-09-05: Record the existing `components.json` evidence (style `new-york`, `tsx`) as the design-system state; selected registry is none; no tokens or brand values are invented; neither `components.json` is edited.

For Blade, store pointers only; tokens are owned by zeroh-design. Not applicable: this repository is non-Blade.

## Consequences

- Positive: `docs/ux-canon.md` links real evidenced homes.
- Negative: visual language remains undecided until brand inputs are supplied.

## Revisit when

A registry, token source or brand input is approved, or either `components.json` changes.
